label: Losing hope
title: Bhagavad Gita for Losing Hope: 7 Verses for Tough Times
description: Seven verses for when nothing seems to work, from Arjuna putting down his bow (1.47) to Krishna's call to stand (2.3). Sanskrit, plain English and one thing to try.
h1: Bhagavad Gita for losing hope: 7 verses for tough times
subtitle: It starts where you might be, sitting down. Read one a day, or all seven tonight.
keywords: bhagavad gita quotes for hard times
gita verses for motivation in difficult times
bhagavad gita verses on losing hope
intro: The Gita's teaching begins at its hero's lowest point. Arjuna puts down his bow and sits in the chariot, unable to go on (1.47). Krishna stays with him. These verses move from that collapse to Krishna's first push to stand, his promise that no one who does good comes to ruin (6.40), the care he offers those who turn to him (9.22), and two practices for days when hope is thin. The last is from the Ramayana: Lakshman sitting with Ram through four months of rain.

days.heading: Even Arjuna sat down
days.line: Arjuna put down his bow and sat in the chariot, too overwhelmed to go on.
days.forYou: The narrator Sanjaya speaks these words. He describes the greatest archer of his time putting down his bow and sitting in the chariot, his mind sunk in sorrow. The Gita begins with someone who can't go on, and it stays with him for seventeen more chapters.
days.today: Tell one person, plainly, that things are hard right now.

days.heading: Stand up
days.line: This smallness of heart does not suit you. Shake it off and stand up.
days.forYou: Krishna's first words of counsel are a push: klaibyaṃ mā sma gamaḥ, don't give in to this weakness of heart; stand up. He says it once, the way a friend would, and then spends the rest of the Gita explaining why. Losing hope is real, and there is more to you than this moment.
days.today: Write down one thing you once managed that was harder than you expected.
days.note: Krishna says this once, as a friend, and then explains for seventeen chapters. Your feelings still count.

days.heading: No one who does good is lost
days.line: Whoever does good never comes to ruin, my friend. Not here, not after.
days.forYou: Arjuna asks what happens to someone who tries and falls short. Krishna answers tenderly, calling him tāta, my dear: whoever does good never comes to a bad end, here or after. What you've tried to do well has not been wasted.
days.today: List three good things you did this year that nobody saw.

days.heading: What you lack, carried
days.line: Turn to me with your whole heart, and I will carry what you lack and guard what you have.
days.forYou: Yoga-kṣemaṃ vahāmy aham: Krishna says he carries what those who turn to him lack and guards what they have. Bills still need paying and plans still need making. The verse invites you to stop carrying all of it alone.
days.today: Hand one worry over, in prayer, to a friend, or on paper, and agree not to pick it up again today.
days.note: Trust eases worry. Keep doing your part and planning well.

days.heading: Be on your own side
days.line: Be on your own side. Lift yourself up, don't push yourself down. You can be your own friend.
days.forYou: Uddhared ātmanātmānam: lift yourself by yourself, and don't push yourself down. In hard times the harshest voice is often our own. Krishna asks you to be your own friend, and Arjuna himself shows that asking for help is part of that.
days.today: Speak to yourself today the way you'd speak to a friend in your situation.

days.heading: With a heart that doesn't give up
days.line: Yoga is unhooking from sorrow. Practise it with resolve and a heart that doesn't lose hope.
days.forYou: Krishna calls yoga the unhooking from sorrow and says to practise it with resolve, anirviṇṇa-cetasā: with a mind that doesn't lose heart. Hope here is something you do. You carry on, a little each day.
days.today: Pick one small daily action and keep it for a week, whatever your mood.

days.heading: Some seasons are for waiting

story.title: Ram waits out the monsoon
story.body: After Sita was taken, the rains came, and Ram had to wait four months on a mountainside before any search could begin. Nothing could be done. He couldn't sleep for grief. Lakshman sat with him and reminded him that endless grieving drains every purpose, and that this was a season for waiting, not for giving up. Ram resolved to wait well, and when the rains ended, the search began.
story.lesson: Some seasons are for waiting. Wait well, without letting grief take you.

days.forYou: If nothing you do seems to move anything right now, you may be in a monsoon. Monsoons end.
days.today: Name one thing to tend while you wait: your health, a skill, or a friendship.

verse.sanskrit: अलं वीर व्यथां गत्वा न त्वं शोचितुमर्हसि । शोचते ह्यवसीदन्ति सर्वार्था विदितं हि ते ॥
verse.line: Those who keep grieving lose every purpose they had. Don't let sorrow take all of you.

faq.q: What does the Bhagavad Gita say about losing hope?
faq.a: The Gita begins with Arjuna losing hope (1.47). Krishna's first answer is to stand up (2.3). Later he promises that no one who does good comes to ruin (6.40), that he carries the welfare of those who turn to him (9.22), and that yoga should be practised with a heart that doesn't lose courage (6.23).

faq.q: Which Gita verse gives strength in difficult times?
faq.a: Readers often turn to 2.3 (stand up), 6.5 (lift yourself by yourself), 9.22 (I carry what you lack) and 18.66 (do not grieve). This plan uses the first three.

faq.q: What if things feel completely hopeless?
faq.a: Please don't carry it alone. Talk to someone you trust today, and if you're thinking about harming yourself, contact a helpline now. The numbers are below.
